source: arXiv:1610.00278v1, Appendix C / original H1,H-minus-one operator prerequisites for the main theorems
scope: Full original-domain weak Miura factorization and exact eigenspace correspondence with a fixed first-order companion operator. A necessary operator-domain step toward the remaining physical multiplicity/characteristic-order identification.
results: Every original period-two L2 weak solution of v'=u*v+b with u,b in L2 has the full original H1 regularity. The proof derives ell^(4/3), then ell1, then the L2 derivative. The recovered H1 representative has exactly the original raw coefficients and satisfies the actual first-order differential operator equation.

Young convolution commutes with translation and with the actual Wiener right convolution action for every admissible Young triple, including the L2,L2-to-infinity endpoint. This proves the needed associativity without replacing an infinite convolution by a formal sum.

Native period-two L2, derivative and quadratic-product realizations in the original H-minus-one space retain all raw coefficients, the frequency pi*n, and every smooth-test action. Distributional Leibniz and weak-product associativity hold for arbitrary complex L2 Miura input and full original H1 factors.

The literal original potential u'+u^2 satisfies L(q)f=-(f'-u*f)'-u*(f'-u*f) on EVERY original H1 domain vector, with no derivative, boundedness, reality, endpoint or finite-Fourier-support assumption on u.

For EVERY original inhomogeneous Hill equation with L2 forcing, the actual L2 quasi-derivative belongs to H1 and solves the exact L2 first-order equation. This applies to eigenvectors and to original finite root chains with H1 right-hand sides.
The fixed full-domain companion operator is (f,h) mapped to (i*(h'+u*h),i*(f'-u*f)). Every companion eigenvector at frequency z projects to the original Hill equation at energy z^2, even when z=0.
At z!=0 every original Hill eigenvector has a constructed full H1 companion lift. Projection is a complex-linear bijection of the full eigenspaces; actual geometric multiplicities agree.

If the native Miura potential is real on all smooth tests, previously proved original semisimplicity identifies its actual physical algebraic multiplicity with the fixed companion eigenspace dimension at z!=0.
qualifications: This milestone treats every complex L2 Miura input on the literal native period-two domain. It does not yet prove that every original real H-minus-one potential has a real Miura representation after a suitable spectral translation.

The companion is a fixed actual first-order differential operator, but its constant rotation to the already verified Dirac operator and the corresponding physical characteristic-order transport are still to be proved.

Injectivity and the inverse eigenspace map require z!=0. The later spectral translation must be selected so that the desired energy has a nonzero square root; that selection is not silently assumed for every original potential.
No equality of algebraic root spaces is asserted for arbitrary complex Miura potentials. The algebraic-multiplicity corollary assumes native reality and uses already verified semisimplicity.
The original finite-p inverse spectral input, uniform full-isospectral bound, Theorem2.2/fullLemma2.21, Dirichlet comparison and all main Birkhoff/KdV theorems remain unproved.
publication: Local milestone; GitHub export remains pending explicit destination approval after the earlier automatic review rejection.
